Thanks for the time last week. As we discussed, Acme's renewal is up for Q3 and you indicated interest in expanding the dedicated pool (additional GPUs) and locking in a throughput guarantee for mission-critical workloads. To move procurement forward I attached a draft addendum and a capacity quote. High-level proposal is below:

- Term: 12 months (renewal effective 2026-08-01)
- Dedicated capacity: add 8 x A100-80GB equivalent GPUs to the existing reserved pool (total becomes 24 GPUs)
- Throughput guarantee (reserved pool aggregate): committed baseline of 400,000 tokens/sec sustained, with a burst allowance up to 600,000 tokens/sec for short periods (see SLO language in the addendum)
- Measurement & credits: platform-measured tokens/sec with a 1-minute sliding window; small monthly service credit if measured sustained throughput falls below the agreed threshold (draft language attached)
- Pricing impact: see Capacity_Quote_Acme_2026Q3.xlsx (attached) — pricing reflects reserved hardware + a 12-month commitment discount

Next steps: can you confirm the procurement timeline (legal review window and PO issuance target)? If you want, we can set a 30-minute call with Marcus (infra) and Marissa (AM) to walk the SLO wording and measurement specifics.

Samir —

Appreciate the clear follow-up. Below is a concise, procurement-friendly summary and sample SLO language you can hand to legal. I also attached an updated addendum (RWD_Addendum_v1.2.pdf) with the clauses inserted.

Measurement point and window
- Measurement: aggregate tokens/second is measured at the Redwood serving gateway egress for the customer's routed traffic across the dedicated pool. This measurement counts tokens emitted by the model(s) served under the customer's account.
- Window: a 1-minute sliding window sampled at 10-second intervals (platform default).

SLO (sample wording) — RESERVED POOL THROUGHPUT GUARANTEE
- Commitment: Redwood will use commercially reasonable efforts to provide an aggregate sustained throughput for Acme Analytics of 400,000 tokens/second ("Committed Throughput") across the reserved pool during the Term.
- Burst allowance: the reserved pool supports bursts up to 600,000 tokens/second for up to 30 consecutive seconds, subject to available capacity and existing reservations.
- Measurement and breach: A breach is recorded when the measured 1-minute sliding-window tokens/sec falls below 90% of the Committed Throughput (i.e., below 360,000 tokens/sec) for two (2) or more non-overlapping 1-minute windows in a calendar day.

Remediation and credits
- Remedy: On a confirmed breach, Redwood will (a) provide immediate mitigation actions (traffic routing to alternate compatible model variants or temporary capacity reallocation) and (b) issue a service credit.
- Credit calculation (example): For each calendar day with a breach, Redwood will credit Acme 0.5% of that month's reserved capacity charge for each breached 10-minute interval, up to a maximum cumulative credit of 25% of the monthly reserved capacity charge. Example: if in July there are four breached 10-minute intervals, credit = 4 * 0.5% = 2% of July's reserved charge.

Operational notes
- Root cause & reporting: Redwood will provide an incident summary and throughput measurement logs for the affected windows within five (5) business days of confirming a breach.
- Capacity scaling: If Acme expects regularly sustained load above Committed Throughput, cadence-based autoscale options (additional reserved GPUs) can be added mid-term; pricing and lead times are in the attached quote.

Marcus (cc'd) — for the record, the quoted 8 x A100-equivalent GPUs added to the pool are sized to meet ~400k tokens/sec sustained for Acme's typical mix (40–60 token per request median). If your traffic profile differs, we can re-run the sizing.

Next steps
- If this language aligns with Acme's legal, we can prep a redline and send a DocuSign envelope for the addendum. Jordan, can you confirm final pricing and expiration on the quote?

Thanks,
